//: The hand-written data the one-time copy (scripts/copy-from-redis.ts) moves into the database, from the files #290 part 2b deletes.
wishlist: the 39 entries src/data/wishlist.ts held, as games rows, their box art included (`npm run box-art` rewrites each `image`); also the wishlist fixture for tests and e2e.
awards: every hand-written award win, wishlist and collection, by BoardGameGeek id; the copy keeps those BGG does not list as owner_awards.
honoursFrom: a later edition whose honours are its original edition's (Dominion, Love Letter).
collection: the BGG ids of src/data/games.ts and the games inside its games, whose BoardGameGeek data the copy fetches.
The awards, honoursFrom and collection parts go with the copy, in a follow-up once production has run it.

wishlist.name: Lost Cities
wishlist.description: An elegant two-player card game of expeditions. Do you commit or hold back? Deceptively tense, quick, and endlessly replayable — the head-to-head filler you don't own yet.
wishlist.video: how to play Lost Cities board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Nemesis
wishlist.description: Cinematic sci-fi survival on an alien-infested spaceship. Semi-cooperative with secret objectives — expect tension, betrayal, and dramatic deaths.
wishlist.video: how to play Nemesis board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Blood on the Clocktower
wishlist.description: The most acclaimed social deduction game ever made. 100+ roles, a storyteller mechanic, and dead players who stay active. Perfect for 10–15 people.
wishlist.video: how to play Blood on the Clocktower tutorial

wishlist.name: Splendor
wishlist.description: Collect gem tokens, buy development cards, and attract nobles. Deceptively simple engine-building with beautiful components and surprisingly deep decisions.
wishlist.video: how to play Splendor board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Wyrmspan
wishlist.description: Wingspan's dragon-taming cousin. Excavate caves, entice dragons into your lair, and chain their abilities into an engine. Familiar rhythm, deeper decisions, gorgeous art.
wishlist.video: how to play Wyrmspan board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Wyrmspan: Dragon Academy
wishlist.description: The first Wyrmspan expansion. Eighty new dragons and 25 caves, fledglings you train up for bonuses and points, new dragon guilds and objectives, and a round tracker that offers an income choice when you pass. Requires the base game.
wishlist.video: Wyrmspan Dragon Academy expansion how to play

wishlist.name: Dominion: Seaside
wishlist.description: Dominion's second expansion, about planning a turn ahead. Duration cards stay in play and pay out again at the start of your next turn, and mats set cards aside for later. The 2022 Second Edition has 27 Kingdom cards, swapping eight first-edition cards for nine new ones and doubling the Durations to sixteen. Requires the base game.
wishlist.video: how to play Dominion Seaside second edition

wishlist.name: Dominion: Prosperity
wishlist.description: Dominion's big-money expansion. Platinum and Colony sit above Gold and Province, Treasures come with abilities of their own, and Victory point tokens reward decks that score as they go. The 2022 Second Edition keeps 25 Kingdom cards, nine of them new. Requires the base game.
wishlist.video: how to play Dominion Prosperity second edition

wishlist.name: Catan: Seafarers
wishlist.description: Catan goes to sea. Ships run across the water like roads to reach new islands, gold fields pay out any resource you choose, and a pirate blocks shipping the way the robber blocks land. Instead of one random board it comes with a book of scenarios to play through. Requires the Catan base game; a separate extension adds five and six players.
wishlist.video: how to play Catan Seafarers expansion tutorial

wishlist.name: Harmonies
wishlist.description: Stack colourful tokens into mountains, rivers, and forests, then welcome animals to the landscapes you've built. A serene puzzle with real spatial bite in under an hour.
wishlist.video: how to play Harmonies board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Zombie Burrito
wishlist.description: Throw Throw Burrito's undead sequel. Match cards, grab the burrito, and throw it at your friends — now with zombie infections and a tent to hide in. Loud, fast, and chaotic.
wishlist.video: how to play Zombie Burrito game tutorial

wishlist.name: Everdell
wishlist.description: Build a woodland city of critters and constructions beneath the Ever Tree. Worker placement meets tableau-building with cards that combo beautifully and a board that stands up.
wishlist.video: how to play Everdell board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Exploding Kittens: The Board Game
wishlist.description: The card game grows a board. Move around a kitten-themed track, collect and play cards, and dodge the explosions — same silly energy, more room to scheme.
wishlist.video: Exploding Kittens The Board Game how to play

wishlist.name: 7 Wonders Duel
wishlist.description: 7 Wonders rebuilt for exactly two. Draft from a pyramid of cards, race for science or military supremacy, and build wonders before your rival does. Tense, sharp, and 30 minutes.
wishlist.video: how to play 7 Wonders Duel tutorial

wishlist.name: dnup
wishlist.description: A fast, clever shedding card game where every card has two values and flipping your hand changes them all. Play sets, outbid the table, and be first to empty your hand. Quick, portable, and addictive for 2–5.
wishlist.video: how to play dnup card game tutorial

wishlist.name: Sky Team
wishlist.description: Pilot and co-pilot land a plane together by placing dice on the cockpit — lower the gear, deploy flaps, brake, keep it level — with no talking once the round starts. Each airport is a new scenario. Fifteen tense minutes a landing.
wishlist.video: how to play Sky Team board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Star Realms
wishlist.description: Head-to-head deck-building in 20 minutes. Both players start with the same weak fleet and buy ships and bases from a shared row to batter the other's authority to zero. Faction combos reward specialising. Fits in a pocket.
wishlist.video: how to play Star Realms tutorial

wishlist.name: The Crew: The Quest for Planet Nine
wishlist.description: Trick-taking like Hearts, but everyone wins or loses together. Each of 50 missions hands specific players tasks such as 'win the blue 4' or 'take no tricks', and you can barely communicate. Twenty minutes a mission — you'll play three in a row.
wishlist.video: how to play The Crew Quest for Planet Nine tutorial

wishlist.name: Pandemic Legacy: Season 1
wishlist.description: Pandemic as a year-long story over 12 to 24 sessions. Cities scar permanently, characters gain relationships and can die, sealed boxes open with new rules, and stickers change the board forever. Regularly called the best board game ever designed. Play it with one fixed group.
wishlist.video: how to play Pandemic Legacy Season 1 tutorial

wishlist.name: Bomb Busters
wishlist.description: Each player holds a rack of numbered wires facing out — you see everyone's but your own. Cut a wire by naming a number you think a teammate holds; a wrong guess costs a detonator. Sixty-six missions add gadgets and traps as the campaign ramps up.
wishlist.video: how to play Bomb Busters board game tutorial

wishlist.name: MicroMacro: Crime City
wishlist.description: A giant black-and-white poster shows a city frozen in time. Sixteen cases ask you to find a body, then track victim and suspects backward across the map to reconstruct the crime. Works with kids, grandparents, and anyone who loved Where's Wally.
wishlist.video: how to play MicroMacro Crime City tutorial

wishlist.name: Wingspan
wishlist.description: Attract birds to your forest, grassland, and wetland by paying food and eggs. Each bird has a real-world fact and a power that fires whenever you use its habitat, so your board becomes an engine that lays eggs, caches food, and draws cards. Gorgeous production with a birdfeeder dice tower.
wishlist.video: how to play Wingspan board game tutorial

wishlist.name: The Quacks of Quedlinburg
wishlist.description: You're a quack doctor brewing a potion by pulling ingredient chips blindly from your bag. Each chip moves you up your cauldron for points, but too many cherry bombs and it explodes. Buy better ingredients between rounds. Loud, tense, and a hit with the Exploding Kittens crowd.
wishlist.video: how to play Quacks of Quedlinburg tutorial

wishlist.name: Cascadia
wishlist.description: Take a paired habitat tile and wildlife token from the market and add them to your slice of the Pacific Northwest. Each animal scores in its own pattern — bears in pairs, salmon in runs — and the scoring cards change every game. Calm, quick, and the same weight as Azul.
wishlist.video: how to play Cascadia board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Survive the Island
wishlist.description: The 2024 remake of the classic Survive: Escape from Atlantis. Your island is sinking tile by tile and you need to get your explorers to the corner islands by boat or by swimming — past sharks, whales, and sea serpents that the other players steer at you. Cutthroat, quick to teach, and 45 minutes of glee for 2–5.
wishlist.video: how to play Survive the Island board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Akropolis
wishlist.description: Take three-hex tiles from a market and stack them to build a Greek city upward. Houses want to cluster, temples want to be surrounded, and building higher multiplies your score. Twenty-five minutes and instantly teachable.
wishlist.video: how to play Akropolis board game tutorial

wishlist.name: SETI: Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence
wishlist.description: Launch probes, orbit planets on a rotating solar-system board, and scan for signals. Midway through you discover alien species that bolt on whole new rule modules. Real science, one to four players, and two to three hours for a full evening.
wishlist.video: how to play SETI board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Ark Nova
wishlist.description: Build a modern zoo by playing animal cards into enclosures, backing conservation projects, and hiring staff. Two scoring tracks move toward each other and the game ends when they cross. Two to three hours with 255 unique cards.
wishlist.video: how to play Ark Nova board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Terraforming Mars
wishlist.description: Corporations raise the temperature, oxygen, and ocean count on Mars by playing project cards from a deck of over 200, placing cities and forests on a shared hex map. About two hours, with a solo mode and a well-loved app.
wishlist.video: how to play Terraforming Mars tutorial

wishlist.name: The Mind
wishlist.description: Cards numbered 1 to 100 are dealt out. Together you must play them in ascending order with no talking, no signals, and no turn order. Somehow groups learn to feel the timing. Weird, quick, and unforgettable.
wishlist.video: how to play The Mind card game tutorial

wishlist.name: Wavelength
wishlist.description: A hidden dial sits somewhere on a spectrum like 'hot to cold' or 'overrated to underrated'. One player gives a clue — 'coffee' — and their team argues about where it belongs. Plays two to twelve, and the arguments are the game.
wishlist.video: how to play Wavelength board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Just One
wishlist.description: One player closes their eyes. Everyone else writes a single-word clue for a mystery word, but duplicated clues are wiped before the guesser looks. Fully cooperative, taught in one sentence, and thirteen rounds take twenty minutes.
wishlist.video: how to play Just One board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Decrypto
wishlist.description: Each team has four secret words. One player gives clues so their team can guess a three-digit code, but the other team hears every clue and tries to intercept the pattern. Codenames' sharper, tenser cousin.
wishlist.video: how to play Decrypto board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Flip 7
wishlist.description: Flip cards one at a time to add to your score, but a duplicate number busts you. Flip seven unique cards and the round ends with a bonus. Push-your-luck that works with any number of people and takes five minutes to teach.
wishlist.video: how to play Flip 7 card game tutorial

wishlist.name: Sounds Fishy
wishlist.description: A bluffing party game built on questions nobody knows the answer to. One player holds the true answer and everyone else improvises a fake; the guesser flips fish tokens one at a time, trying to weed out every Red Herring before landing on the True Blue Kipper. Quick to teach, 20 minutes, and best with a big table.
wishlist.video: how to play Sounds Fishy party game tutorial

wishlist.name: Glyphics
wishlist.description: Charades for people who can't draw. Pick a prompt from your card and build it out of the forty-odd plastic shapes in the box while the table has sixty seconds to shout out what it is — builder and guesser both score, and phrases are worth double. By Eric Olsen, who went on to design Flip 7, and it takes as many players as you can fit round the table.
wishlist.video: how to play Glyphics board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Lovestruck
wishlist.description: A reality dating show as a social deduction game. Every contestant swears they are looking for love, but some are only chasing screen time — go on dates, play action cards to stir up love or drama, and work out who means it before the season finale makes you couple up. Guess wrong, or let the viewing figures hit ten million, and the fame-hunters win. Five to ten players, and the table talk is the whole game.
wishlist.video: how to play Lovestruck board game tutorial

wishlist.name: Herd Mentality
wishlist.description: A question is read out, everyone writes an answer in secret, and the goal is to agree with the herd rather than be right. Match the most common answer and you take a cow; be the only one who went your own way and you are stuck with the Pink Cow, which stops you winning until someone else earns it. First to eight cows wins. Nothing to teach, twenty minutes, and it plays from four to twenty, so it holds up when the whole party wants in.
wishlist.video: how to play Herd Mentality party game tutorial

wishlist.name: Two Rooms and a Boom
wishlist.description: Two teams, two rooms, one bomb. Everyone is secretly Red or Blue: Blue protects the President, and Red wins if the Bomber ends up in the same room as the President when the last round runs out. Over a few short timed rounds each room picks a leader who sends hostages across, while you decide who gets a look at your card and who you are lying to. Six to thirty players, so it only gets better the bigger the party.
wishlist.video: how to play Two Rooms and a Boom tutorial
